note: Chains of events that have played out before. Steps with a 'check' light up from the data; steps without one are news to watch for. Likelihoods are judgment calls from the history cited.

scenarios.title: El Niño dries out Asia's harvests
scenarios.why: NOAA (12 Nov) says El Niño is still strengthening, with better than a 79% chance it stays strong through March 2027 and about a 60% chance it becomes one of the strongest on record. Sugar is already up 28% in 3 months.

steps.text: A strong El Niño forms in the Pacific
Dry, hot weather in Indonesia, Malaysia, India, Thailand and Australia
steps.watch: drought and weak-monsoon news from those countries

steps.text: Sugar and rice prices climb
Palm oil output falls and cooking oil jumps 25% or more in a year

scenarios.history: In all 5 strong El Niños since 1990, cooking oils cost more a year after the peak: 2% and 9% more after the two in the 1990s, and 27% to 55% more after the last three.

scenarios.title: La Niña follows and hits the Americas
scenarios.why: After 7 of the 9 strong El Niños since 1950, the Pacific swung to La Niña within 18 months.

steps.text: El Niño peaks and starts to fade
The Pacific flips cool: La Niña
Drought in Argentina, southern Brazil and the southern US
steps.watch: crop-condition news from Argentina and the US Plains

steps.text: Soybean and maize prices rise 20% or more in a year

scenarios.history: The 2020-23 La Niña lasted three winters in a row. In the last one, a drought cut Argentina's soybean harvest to the smallest in more than 20 years.

scenarios.title: Expensive oil leaks into food
scenarios.why: Oil alone is a weak guide: after the 6 oil spikes this size since 1990, food was higher a year later 3 times and lower 3 times. Oil is now easing and world food prices fell for a third month in October, but El Niño could still give the second push.

steps.text: Oil spikes
Diesel, shipping and farm costs rise
steps.watch: diesel and freight prices in the news

steps.text: Crops that double as fuel (biodiesel, ethanol) get pricier
World food prices climb 10% or more in a year

scenarios.history: 2021-22: oil doubled, then Russia invaded Ukraine. World food prices rose 35% in a year to their all-time record.

scenarios.title: High oil prices cure themselves
scenarios.why: Raised this week. Oil fell about 20% in early November as fears of new strikes on Iran eased, and the IEA sees a growing oil surplus. A fresh attack on Hormuz shipping could reverse it.

steps.text: Oil spikes
People drive less, businesses cut back, producers pump more
steps.watch: OPEC output decisions and talk of a slowdown

steps.text: Oil falls 20% or more from its recent high
Gas, shipping and food costs ease

down: Copper, if it comes with a recession
scenarios.history: 2008: oil averaged $134 in July and $42 in December as the financial crisis hit. Copper fell by almost two thirds over the same months.

scenarios.title: An export ban sets off a scramble
scenarios.why: Governments limit food exports when prices at home jump, and staple prices are up sharply this year. India sells about a quarter of the world's traded rice, Russia about a fifth of its wheat.

steps.text: A staple jumps 25% or more in a year
A top seller limits exports to keep food cheap at home
steps.watch: export bans, quotas or taxes from India (rice) or Russia (wheat)

steps.text: Buyers panic and prices spike 20% or more in 3 months
Countries that rely on one seller get hit hardest
steps.watch: the buyers shown in Who feeds whom, below

scenarios.history: 2008: rice nearly tripled in six months as India and Vietnam limited exports. 2010: wheat rose 56% in two months after Russia's drought and export ban. 2023: rice rose 24% in two months after India's ban.

scenarios.title: Cheap fertilizer means bigger harvests
scenarios.why: After the 7 fertilizer crashes this size since 1975, maize was cheaper a year later in 5. This pulls the other way from El Niño and expensive oil.

steps.text: Fertilizer prices crash
Farmers fertilize more for the 2027 planting season
Bigger harvests
steps.watch: harvest estimates from the USDA and FAO

steps.text: Grain prices fall 10% or more in 6 months

scenarios.history: Early 2023: urea had fallen by two thirds from its 2022 peak. A year later, maize was 33% cheaper and wheat 26% cheaper.
